messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • High GPU queue for service=redwood-generation-prod — event=evt-2087654321 | queue_est=~11k | p99=18.2s | autoscaler=failed_max_nodes_reached
ops-bot: automated note: investigated pods pending due to Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
oncall-erica: acknowledged. I'm on-call and taking lead. Pinging infra and platform. @maya @oliver please advise next steps
maya: quick triage — show `kubectl get pods -n inference`? are pods Pending or Evicted?
sam: pasted minimal output:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS    AGE
gen-model-v2-566c7f8d6-abcde       0/1     Pending   0           3m
gen-model-v2-566c7f8d6-fghij       0/1     Pending   3m
... many Pending (Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu)
```
oliver: checked autoscaler logs: scaleUp aborted — nodePool=gpu-prod-pool at configured maxNodes=40
li: `kubectl describe pod gen-model-v2-566c7f8d6-abcde` shows event: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu." — yep, nodepool quota is the blocker
oncall-erica: customer impact? which endpoints/orgs affected?
kaya: support triage — streaming endpoints returning 5xx for high-traffic tenants (acme-inc, beta-qa), many timeouts at 60s. Error rate +15% last 10m. CS queued top-ten notice
maya: mitigation options (prioritized): 1) Manual node-pool bump (fast) — needs cloud quota + ops approval 2) Route noncritical traffic to cpu fallback or lower-quality model 3) Enable emergency batch mode to accept backlog with TTL extension 4) Cross-region failover for permissive tenants
oliver: opening cloud request to increase gpu-prod-pool 40->48 now. Will ping cloud-ops. Ticket will include justification and cost center
sam: before manual resize lands, can we quickly throttle experimental/internal traffic to free capacity? Suggest rate-limiting tag=experimental on generate route
li: low-risk nginx limit we can flip now:
```
# limit experimental orgs to 10r/s
map $http_x_org_tag $limit_key {
  default "";
  experimental "$remote_addr";
}
limit_req_zone $limit_key zone=exp:10m rate=10r/s;
```
(oncall-erica) do it — minimize blast radius
kaya: drafting status page note: will notify CS + prepare customer email template. ETA 4-6m
ops-bot: autoscaler unchanged for 3m. Cloud provider message: "Node pool gpu-prod-pool at quota limit"
oliver: cloud console request submitted: CLD-98122. Cloud warns: project quota cores=320 nearing limit; finance approval required for >+20% spend
maya: can we fallback for low-SLA orgs to gen-model-v1-quant? degrades perf but saves GPU time
li: yes, router patch ready. snippet:
```
- route: generation
  condition: org.sla == "low"
  model: gen-model-v2
+ route: generation
  condition: org.sla == "low"
  model: gen-model-v1-quant
```
oncall-erica: two-track: A) throttle experimental (sam/li) B) request manual node bump (oliver) C) route low-tier to fallback (maya) D) status posted (kaya)
sam: throttle rule applied to edge for header tag=experimental. Observability confirms reduced ingress from flagged orgs
oliver: cloud console accepted request but flagged project quota. Escalating to cloud-ops on-call. @zara_cloud tagged
zara_cloud: looking now. Quick check: eu-west-1 has spare capacity (approx 12 GPUs) — can we route some permissive tenants there?
maya: yes, we can split traffic. I'll stage 30% of eligible traffic to eu-west (orgs with flexible latency SLO)
li: applied feature-flag `--route-split generation:eu-west=30%`. Monitoring: queue length down ~35% and p99 for those tenants +1.2s
kaya: published status.v1 to status.redwood.com/incidents/2087654321: "GPU capacity constraints affecting some generation requests. Mitigations in progress." CS notified top-ten customers
ops-bot: cloud-ops updated: temporary quota bump approved to allow resize to 48 nodes, pending execution
oliver: executing resize CLI now:
```
gcloud container clusters resize redwood-prod --node-pool gpu-prod-pool --num-nodes 48 --region us-central1
Operation started... completed successfully.
```
ops-bot: cluster node count increased to 48. New nodes joining and kube-scheduler placing pods
sam: pods transitioning from Pending -> Running. `kubectl get pods -n inference` shows gen-model-v2 replicas healthy
kaya: metrics: error rate decreasing, p99 trending back to baseline over 10-12m. Status updated: "Partial mitigation: capacity added and traffic rerouted. Monitoring continues."
maya: follow-ups and action items:
1) increase autoscaler headroom from 10% -> 20% to avoid tight ceiling
2) add an auto-fallback routing rule: if global_queue > 2k then route low-tier to quantized variant
3) formal postmortem in 48h including cost/SLA tradeoffs and quota mitigation plan
oncall-erica: creating INC-2087654321, owner @maya. Also add RBAC shortcut and runbook for rapid manual node bump to reduce handoffs
oliver: note: long-term action — request permanent quota increase with cloud provider and add cross-region spare pools for surge capacity
kaya: CS has emailed top-ten customers with template. No exec-level escalation needed at this time
maya: closing active paging loop. We'll monitor for 2h. Reopen if regressions appear. Thanks all :thumbsup:
